title: So Much Extra Storage Space
body:
This over-the-door organizer is a great way to add storage without taking up any floor space. The six shelves are roomy and hold much more than I expected, while the mesh side pockets are perfect for keeping smaller items organized and easy to see. The materials are durable, and it hangs stably on the back of my door.
It feels sturdy when loaded, and the neutral beige color looks clean and unobtrusive. I like that it can be used for so many different things — shoes, purses or extra closet storage. With six shelves and 13 additional pockets, you get a lot of useful storage for the price, making it a great value for the money.

title: Easy Sturdy Extra Storage
body:
This is a great six-tier over the door organizer with roomy compartments and some thoughtful design features. Quick and easy to assemble, with plastic (not cardboard) inserts for the shelf floors. Mesh sides allow you to easily see shelf contents, and there are also additional mesh pockets added on the side and top for even more storage. The metal hooks that go over the door have a spring piece on them that helps hold them up against the door.
One thing that might have been nice is some sort of padding on the metal door hooks to help hold it in place from sliding side to side and keep it from scratching the door surface. This is a great low-cost solution for adding some extra storage in a space.

title: NO HANG-UPS WITH THIS HANG UP STORAGE
body:
Being the organizer and leader of a large social bicycle club here in Fort Lauderdale with over 1550 members and growing daily, the safety, health and well-being of our riders is always priority one. The same goes for our mounts as well. It is discussed before every slow roll. And one thing all my members know about me is that I love customization and personalization. And if it serves both safety and customization then roll on I say! My local bike shop could tell you how much they make from our patronage. And not just for technical stuff but for lots of other fun stuff as well, gadgets and accessories are always welcome. I like to gift away some small safety item to our new members at the beginning of each slow roll, most often it will be a safety whistle to wear while riding. Sometimes the gifting goes to another level. It might be a lighting kit, a set of pedals or grips, locking kits, occasionally even a pair of gloves or a helmet. I encourage my members to keep their mounts very well maintained in order to not get left behind (in reality we would never let anyone get left behind). Anything that keeps you out of danger is for us. So I have a bevy of bike gadgets, toys and accessories to gift away before each slow roll. The question is where do I keep all of these items until each months scheduled ride. I have been using plastic bins and boxes. But even with all of this storage I end up with piles of parts on the floor. But now with this JARLINK Over the Door Organizer I have plenty of extra storage space. The height is definitely appropriate for my needs and available space. The pockets have a solid floor and a screened faces-so I can see what is in each pocket without having to dig through them. The design is clever and the manufacturing solid and definitely a quality product. The storage is so well thought out, I expect that it is built to last. The only issue I can see right now is the depth of the shelves. If you plan to use this as a behind the door hanger then you must account for the depth of the shelves not allowing the door to fully open against the wall. The space it takes needs to be considered. But in my case I will not be using this on a door. I will be hooking this up directly to the wall in a good spot and let it hang that way. Will probably use some drywall hook inserts. you must also account for the weight of the items you plan to store. Overall very excited about the new storage space. Will definitely recommend this to my club members. And as always remember:
Ride Safe, Ride Strong, Ride Happy!!

title: Sturdy and mostly functional
body:

I like the mesh panels that allow you to see what's inside while still containing those items and providing ventilation. There are others with clear plastic panels that just seem kind of gross.
My only issue with this unit is that the pockets on the side are not elastic or in any way expandable. It's very difficult to get anything to fit in these pockets. That's a bummer—it would be really nice to supplement the larger pockets with space for little items.
I'm also not a fan of the hooks. I understand why they're designed that way, but I find it really unattractive. I would so much rather have multiple hook options so I can choose the one that fits my door. These are, however, better quality than I expected.
Overall, I'm pleased with this shelving unit. I just think there are a few changes that could make it even better.

body: I purchased two of these. One is used in a small bathroom and has helped immensely with storage. The organizer holds its shape, and feels very durable. If you are short though, only put items in the top sections that you may not need regularly. I suggest placing plastic containers in sections that you might want to put items containing liquids or gels so they stand better (and create sections), as well as protect the organizer from possible leaks.
